overall: Atlanta is experiencing a heavily overcast morning (OVC, 100% cloud cover, ceiling only 335m/~1,100 ft), which is significantly suppressing daytime heating — the running max of 78.8°F at 11:39 ET sits well below the NWS official forecast of 88°F. However, temperatures are still rising with a positive velocity of +3.6°F/hr (30-min) and +2.6°F/hr (2-hour), and all timing models point to the true daily peak arriving in the mid-to-late afternoon (predicted ~14.7–16.3h ET), meaning meaningful heating potential remains.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models cluster in a tight 83.9–86.2°F range (HRRR 83.9, ECMWF 85.5, NBM 86.2), uniformly cooler than the NWS text forecast of 88°F, and the persistent low overcast ceiling this morning strongly supports the cooler model guidance. The META bucket model (most reliable) assigns its highest probability mass to 84–85°F (27.2%) and 86–87°F (27.2%), with the INTRADAY model similarly centered on 84–89°F — all models are largely in agreement that the 84–87°F zone is the most likely landing range.
max_temp_prediction: With ~3 hours remaining before the predicted peak and a running max of 78.8°F, continued warming at a decelerating pace (consistent with cloud-suppressed afternoons) points to a high in the 85–86°F range. If clouds break more aggressively toward 'mostly sunny' as the NWS narrative suggests, there is modest upside toward 87–88°F, but the persistently low ceiling and high humidity (dewpoint 68°F) make a full realization of the 88°F NWS forecast unlikely. Confidence is moderate — the NWP model consensus and META distribution both support 85–86°F as the central estimate, with the primary risk being a later, stronger cloud break driving temperatures toward the upper 86–88°F tail.
